excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
<@586161934425128960> thoughts on your comment here https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/958#discussion_r4379733164

I guess by safety of the call delay you mean that the EL will respond as soon as possible.

I am not sure if ELs always have a fully packed and ready to be served payload at hand, so the response delay might include time to finalize the build process (packing + hashing etc); although that should be really fast.

As for the requirement to respond asap, it would be great to have a Hive test to enforce it, if such a test scenario can be implemented in Hive. Before that PR we had a very similar statement in the spec (point (1) of `getPayload`) which ELs didn't adhere to because of the presence of the timeout 🤯 .

Whether it makes sense for CL to delay the call in a situation you have described is a different question imo.

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content:
> I guess by safety of the call delay you mean that the EL will respond as soon as possible.
yes if we know the EL will respond within a few ms, then we can delay `getPayload` until later into the slot and give local payload the same time as builder bids we receive over http or p2p
